text:
maria_prod: :rotating_light: Heads up — canary metric spike in us-west after flipping `new-routing` flag ~10m ago. 5xxs up from 0.2% -> 9% on service-frontend. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/incoming/graph/ABCD1234

deploy-bot: Deploy #5423 for service-frontend completed at 2024-06-18T15:12Z. Canary rollout 20% -> 50% -> 80% scheduled. Health checks started.

sara_oncall: I'm oncall and taking this. Thanks Maria. I'm pulling logs and checking traces. Can someone confirm whether this is user-impacting errors or internal retries? @support_lead can you check any recent CS tickets?

support_lead: quick check — no high-sev customer reports yet, but a handful of 502s from EU test workloads. No billing/customer-facing alerts.

ellie_sre: Traces show upstream 502 from model-proxy with timeout 30s. Error rate correlates with p95 latency jump. Likely connection storm to a newly provisioned pool.

maria_prod: ok let's not escalate yet — plan: immediate flag flip to ride traffic off the new route, then drain canary. Who can flip?

sara_oncall: I'll flip the flag now and then start a gradual traffic siphon. Executing safety command:```/ff toggle new-routing off --reason "canary 5xx spike"```

deploy-bot: Action logged: feature_flag:new-routing set to OFF by sara_oncall at 2024-06-18T15:18Z. Canary weight now 0% (route fallback to stable).

john_platform: Initiating traffic drain runbook steps: 1) confirm flag off, 2) route weights -> stable, 3) scale down canary nodes. Running: `kubectl -n prod set resources deployment/canary --replicas=0`

sara_oncall: Confirmed flag off and traffic shifted. Error rate falling in us-west from 9% -> 1.2% in last 90s. Kicking node drain: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/service-frontend-canary` then scale to 0.

ellie_sre: Observability: no customer-facing 5xxs since weight 0, traces show back to normal stack traces. p95 latency back to baseline. Marking mitigation effective.

support_lead: Notifying ops@redwood and support@redwood about rollback. Drafting customer message template: "We detected increased errors during a canary and reverted the change; no significant customer impact observed." Will post if needed.

maria_prod: Good. Next steps: keep canary disabled for now, open a postmortem to understand root cause (likely model-proxy connection handling under new routing). Assigning to ellie_sre + john_platform + eng-runtime.

sara_oncall: Will monitor for 30m and then hand off to next oncall at 15:45Z. If errors reappear, we will escalate to SEV.

john_platform: Quick note — logs show one backend pool with high connection reset rate, config mismatch on TLS keepalive. Adding a config rollback candidate to the postmortem.

maria_prod: Thanks all. Logging incident in PagerDuty, severity: P2.

sara_oncall: Handoff: I'm leaving the channel at 15:45Z — next oncall is @ellie_sre. Leaving a checklist: flag stays OFF, canary replicas 0, dashboards green, customer comms queued.

ellie_sre: Acknowledged. I'll take 30m watch and then transition to runbook follow-up.

maria_prod: Closing note: rollback verified. No elevated customer impact. Postmortem owners: ellie_sre (lead), john_platform (infra), dev-runtime team. Follow-up sync scheduled 2024-06-19 09:00 PT. :white_check_mark:
